text:
San Jose won this one in overtime, but Florida played the better game and nearly erased a three-goal hole to prove it. The Panthers owned the chances, 3.99 expected goals to 3.56, and the share of simulated replays they win comes to 57 percent. Over 65 minutes, that is the team that deserved the points.

The Sharks built their lead on two special-teams swings from Will Smith. His shorthanded wrist shot in the second period came off a 21 percent chance, and he followed it with a slap shot on the power play less than five minutes later, a 72 percent look that put San Jose up 3-0. Mason Marchment had opened the scoring in the first on a 2 percent chance. Florida pushed back with Eetu Luostarinen on a power play late in the second, and then the third period turned on 17 seconds: Luostarinen tipped one in at 5:01 and Matthew Tkachuk tied it at 5:18. The Panthers outchanced San Jose 1.20 to 0.50 in that period.

Overtime flipped the script. San Jose generated 0.91 expected goals in the extra frame to Florida's none, and Luca Cagnoni finished it at 3:14 on a pass from Smith, with Macklin Celebrini also in on the play. Celebrini had three assists and seven shots, Smith finished with two goals and an assist, and Yaroslav Askarov stopped a bit more than the chances warranted. San Jose cashed in the few big looks it got, and that was the difference.
